title: A struct that owns its invariants

prereqs.why: The methods take &self or &mut self, and which one is the decision being made each time.
bucket_of returns an Option because a value can fall outside, and the caller has to deal with that.
add takes &mut self and calls bucket_of, which takes &self; seeing why that is allowed is part of the exercise.

statement:
Read `lo`, `width` and `n`, then any number of integers.

Build a histogram of `n` buckets, each `width` wide, with bucket `i`
covering `[lo + i*width, lo + (i+1)*width)` — the lower end included,
the upper end not. Values below `lo` and values at or above the top of
the last bucket are counted separately.

Fill in these four methods:

```rust
fn bucket_of(&self, x: i64) -> Option<usize>
fn add(&mut self, x: i64)
fn total(&self) -> u32
fn mode(&self) -> Option<usize>
```

- `bucket_of` is the index, or `None` when the value falls outside.
- `add` counts the value — in its bucket, or as `below` or `above`.
  Every count **saturates** at `u32::MAX` rather than wrapping.
- `total` is everything counted, inside and outside.
- `mode` is the index of the fullest bucket, with the **lowest** index
  winning a tie, or `None` when every bucket is empty.

Then print:

```
buckets <each bucket count, space separated>
outside <below> <above>
total <everything>
mode <index, or the word none>
```

### The sample

```
0 10 4
5 15 25 35 45 -5
```

```
buckets 1 1 1 1
outside 1 1
total 6
mode 0
```

`width` is at least 1 and `n` is at least 1. Values fit in `i64`.
hints: `bucket_of` has two ways to be outside and they are not symmetric. Check `x < lo` first and return early: `(x - lo) / width` on a value below `lo` gives a negative number, and casting that to `usize` gives something enormous rather than something negative.
After the early return, `(x - lo) / width` is non-negative, and the only remaining question is whether it is less than `buckets.len()`.

`add` can call `bucket_of`, even though `add` takes `&mut self` and `bucket_of` takes `&self`: an exclusive borrow can be used where a shared one is wanted. Finish the call before touching the field, though — `self.buckets[self.bucket_of(x).unwrap()] += 1` is the shape that does not compile.
For the mode, skip empty buckets: a histogram where every bucket is zero has no mode, and `None` is how you say that. Strictly greater keeps the lowest index on a tie.
